title: SAT Scatterplots & Lines of Best Fit: Slope, Predictions, and Traps
description:
Scatterplot questions on the SAT come down to one idea: the line of best fit gives predictions, and the dots show what actually happened. This lesson covers the official skill "two-variable data: models and scatterplots," with 6 SAT-style practice questions that get harder as they go.

You'll learn:
• Positive, negative, and no association (and why "always" is a trap)
• How to interpret the slope and y-intercept of a line of best fit in context
• Predicted vs. actual values, and the difference between them
• How to choose a linear or exponential model from a scatterplot or a table
• Interpolation vs. extrapolation: when a prediction can't be trusted
• A test-day method, including when to use Desmos

All questions are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. All data in this video is illustrative (made up for practice). For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank (Problem-Solving and Data Analysis → Two-variable data).
